title: Clear slides, a confident voice and rehearsal that works
course_title: Presentation Skills: Talks, Pitches and Community Meetings

say: Clear slides, a confident voice, and rehearsal that works.
This is the video for module two of Presentation Skills.
Slides should help people understand and remember. They are not your script. Many community talks work better with no slides at all, or one printed sheet.

say: Use Google Slides or Canva, both free on a phone. One idea per slide. If a slide needs two headings, make two slides.

panel.heading: Rules for slides people can read
items: A headline that states the point
Big text: about 28 point or more

say: Give each slide a headline that states the point, plus one picture, number, or up to three short lines. Put your script in the speaker notes.

panel.heading: Rules for slides people can read
items: A headline that states the point

say: Make the text big, about 28 point or more, so the back row can read it.

panel.heading: Rules for slides people can read

say: Use dark text on light, or light on dark. Avoid text over busy photos.

say: Real photos of your own work beat stock pictures. Ask permission before showing anyone's face.

say: And download a PDF copy and keep it on your phone, so you can present even with a poor network.

say: For example, Halima runs a poultry farm near Abuja. Her first slide was titled Our Farm, with eight bullet points about history, birds, feed, vaccines, staff and plans.

panel.heading: Halima's crowded slide, fixed
right: About 60 crates of eggs every week
One photo of crates ready to go

say: She asked: what is the one point? That the farm delivers reliably. Her new headline: we deliver about 60 crates of eggs every week. One photo, one line, and the rest moved to her notes.

say: Slow down, especially in the first minute and on key points. Nerves make most of us rush.

cards.d: Especially in the first minute and on key points. Nerves make you rush.
Speak to the person at the back. Do not drop your volume at the end of sentences.
Pause before and after your main message and key numbers. Silence makes the number land.

say: Speak to the person at the back of the room, and keep your volume up to the end of each sentence.

cards.d: Especially in the first minute and on key points. Nerves make you rush.

say: And pause before and after your key number. Mark a slash in your notes where you will pause. For example: we saved, pause, two hundred and forty thousand naira, pause, in six months.

say: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and your weight even. This stops swaying.

panel.heading: Stand, gesture and look up
items: Hands loose, gestures waist to shoulder
Move only when you change point
Eye contact: one thought, then move on

say: Keep your hands loose, and let them gesture between waist and shoulders. Avoid pockets and folded arms.

panel.heading: Stand, gesture and look up
items: Hands loose, gestures waist to shoulder
Move only when you change point

say: Take a step or two when you change to a new point, then stand still while you make it.

panel.heading: Stand, gesture and look up
items: Hands loose, gestures waist to shoulder
Move only when you change point

say: Look at one person for one full thought, then move to another part of the room. With elders, soften your gaze and read the room. And you do not need to change your accent.

panel.rule: Your accent is fine. Clarity comes from pace and pauses.

panel.rule: Record yourself and fix two habits at a time.

say: How was it, usually gets, it was fine. So give your listener three questions before you start.

panel.heading: Ask three questions, fix in order
items: One thing to keep, one to change
Fix: message, structure, timing, delivery, slides

say: What was my main message? If they cannot say it, your message is not clear.

panel.heading: Ask three questions, fix in order
items: One thing to keep, one to change
Fix: message, structure, timing, delivery, slides

say: Where did you lose interest or get confused?

panel.heading: Ask three questions, fix in order
items: One thing to keep, one to change
Fix: message, structure, timing, delivery, slides

say: And what is one thing to keep doing, and one thing to change? Say thank you, write it down, and do not argue.

panel.heading: Ask three questions, fix in order
items: One thing to keep, one to change
Fix: message, structure, timing, delivery, slides

say: Then fix in this order: message, structure, timing, delivery, and slides last. A beautiful slide cannot save an unclear message. Prepare a short version too, in case your 10 minutes become 4.

say: To remember. One idea per slide, with a PDF back-up. Slow down and pause before key points. Plant your feet. Rehearse aloud with a timer. And fix your message before your slides.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One idea per slide; keep an offline PDF
Slow down, project, pause before key points
Plant your feet; move with purpose
Rehearse aloud, standing, with a timer
Fix message and structure before slides

say: Now build a five-slide deck and save the PDF. Record two takes of your talk and compare them. Then rehearse for one to three people with the three questions.
